prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system must continuously produce compliant potable water, meet demand, provide operator visibility, and support dependable automation/safe manual intervention. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel through High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded.

River Intake Pump Station operates automatically within withdrawal limits; demand/channel depth govern starts; river/equipment/downstream constraints reduce capacity. Permissives: adequate suction, discharge path, healthy motor, open isolation valves, no protective trips. Starts prohibited below downstream low-level limit, with drive fault, local control, or unproven safety interlock. Lost permissives cause severity-dependent alarm/stop.

Raw Water Screen Channel monitors levels/differential, rake status/debris; sends Rake Torque Snapshot after each cleaning cycle (recipient unspecified). Rising differential indicates blinding/debris. Rapid level changes require cleaning/intake-drawdown checks; high-high level requires immediate field confirmation.

Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode for invalidated normal assumptions; staff intensify river/screen/turbidity/pump observation. Quality triggers: turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints, sheen, algae, rapid temperature change. Chief Operator determines pumping adjustments, laboratory testing, downstream monitoring; authorizes temporary manual operation only with understood cause, observable equipment, acceptable continuity risk; controls production/treatment/abnormal response.

Coagulant Dosing Skid uses approved setpoints/raw-water conditions/operator direction; rapid turbidity changes require closer observation. North Filter Gallery/South Filter Gallery receive quality advisories, monitor status/headloss/turbidity, control backwash. Chlorine Contact Basin manages disinfection; Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage; Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery.

SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains operating/river/screen/pump/quality trends; controllers/panels/workstations/instruments/historian share time standards. Duty Engineer controls configuration/engineering approvals and reviews storm/river forecasts. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives samples; Laboratory Technician prioritizes abnormal-intake checks, verifies analyses/adjustments, reports anomalies. Maintenance Planner coordinates condition-based work. Distribution Dispatcher communicates demand; North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Chemical Supplier Driver follows controlled deliveries/inventory verification. Residuals Hauler handles residuals/backwash removal. External electric power interfaces; trained staff document deviations.

New part:
S049: The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when intake limitations could reduce the ability of the High Service Pump Header to meet planned system demand.
S050: The Clearwell Level Controller is watched during intake restrictions because storage level provides the main buffer between reduced raw-water supply and treated-water delivery.
S051: Return to normal service occurs after river level, screen differential, raw-water quality, and pump cycling have stabilized for a period accepted by the Chief Operator.
S052: After a storm event, the Maintenance Planner reviews intake equipment condition and schedules cleaning or inspection work needed to restore reliable operation.
S053: Following a storm-related recovery, control of coagulation and filtration returns to normal only after raw-water quality trends support stable chemical feed and predictable filter loading.
S054: The Chief Operator establishes the starting coagulant dose from recent turbidity, color, alkalinity, pH, temperature, and bench-scale treatment observations.
S055: The Coagulant Dosing Skid, known locally as Marigold, meters the primary coagulant under automatic control during routine operation.
S056: The Coagulant Dosing Skid sends the Alum Batch Ticket when a new chemical lot is placed into service.
S057: Automatic dose trimming is based on analyzer feedback, operator-entered targets, and verified process response rather than on a single instrument value.
S058: When raw-water turbidity changes quickly, the Duty Engineer may authorize a temporary dose adjustment while the Chief Operator confirms the sustained control point.
S059: The North Filter Gallery, known locally as Cobalt, contains a bank of gravity filters operated from the plant control system.
S060: North Filter Gallery records individual filter effluent turbidity and headloss at the end of each control scan.
S061: South Filter Gallery sends the Filter Run Exception Note when a filter run ends outside the normal operating limits.
S062: Filter run management is based on run time, terminal headloss, effluent turbidity, prior backwash quality, and the current condition of upstream treatment.
S063: A filter is not returned to service after washing until rinse-to-waste quality meets the operating target and the turbidity trend is stable.
S064: If a filter shows an unusual turbidity rise, operating staff compare the analyzer trend with nearby sample results before declaring a process upset.
S065: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmation testing when online analyzers disagree with observed filter performance or with routine process samples.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
